guidance: Planning estimate—verify assumptions and important results before committing time or money.
method: Production and location are trimmed, control characters are replaced with spaces and whitespace is collapsed; production is required and both are limited to 80 characters. The shoot date is optional and must be a real Gregorian date in YYYY-MM-DD form, including 29 February in leap years. First shot is a 24-hour HH:MM time. Setup is 0-240 minutes and must not push the crew call before midnight. Scenes run back to back from the first shot, each 1-600 whole minutes, with at most 40 scenes. The meal time is the crew call plus 3-8 hours and may not fall before the first shot. When the schedule reaches the meal time a 15-90 minute meal is inserted: a scene in progress is split, the meal takes its place and the scene resumes afterwards; a meal is not scheduled when the day wraps before the meal time. Wrap is the end of the last scene plus a 0-120 minute wrap-down, and a schedule that would end more than a day past midnight is refused. All arithmetic is in whole minutes, and times display in 24-hour form with a +1 marker past midnight. The tool plans a schedule from durations the user supplies: it does not know travel, lighting changes, overtime rules or meal-penalty rules, and it stores and transmits nothing.
